name: Bulgarian Split Squat
summary: A unilateral lower-body exercise where the rear foot is elevated on a bench or platform to challenge the quads, glutes, and balance of the front leg.

setup: Stand about two to three feet in front of a flat bench or sturdy knee-height platform facing away from it.
Reach one foot back and rest the top of your foot or your toes on the bench.
Keep your torso upright, your hips square to the front, and your front foot planted firmly on the floor with weight distributed across the midfoot and heel.
steps: Lower your body under control by bending the front knee and hip, descending until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground and your back knee approaches the floor.
Maintain a slight, natural forward torso lean while bracing your core.
Drive through the midfoot of your front leg to extend the hip and knee, returning to the starting standing position.
Complete the desired repetitions on one side before switching legs.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower down into the squat, and exhale as you drive through your front foot to return to the top.
cues: Drop the back knee straight down
Keep your front knee tracking over your toes

common_faults.fault: Stance too narrow, causing the front heel to lift off the floor during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Hop or step the front foot slightly further forward to allow full-foot contact throughout the rep.

common_faults.fault: Putting too much weight into the rear elevated leg, causing cramping or hip flexor strain.
common_faults.correction: Focus on keeping roughly eighty to ninety percent of your bodyweight loaded onto your lead leg.

common_faults.fault: Front knee collapsing inward (valgus) during the ascent.
common_faults.correction: Engage the hip abductors and consciously push the knee slightly outward in line with the second and third toes.

precautions: Ensure the elevation surface is secure and will not slide.
Maintain balance by fixing your gaze on an immovable point at eye level.
